input.context: We are about to ship the Bun runtime adoption (ADR-002): Bun 1.3+ replaces Node for the dev/CI test runner; Node 22.6+ remains the consumer runtime. The decision is based on a spike showing 22% wall-time improvement (16.5s vs 21.1s) with bun test --parallel --timeout 30000. What could go wrong in the next 6 months?
constraints: Cannot revert Bun without a visible 20%+ regression signal — reverting adds 2-day overhead
Windows CI must pass — Bun 1.3.14 was the tested build
Consumer runtime stays on Node; Bun is dev/CI only
Escape hatch (test:node script) must remain working

expected_output.summary: Five risk categories: (1) Bun version drift on Windows, (2) test isolation breakage between bun test --parallel workers, (3) Bun subtest shim regression (the NotImplementedError that made initial spike red), (4) CI setup-bun action lagging behind Bun 1.3.x minor releases, (5) contributor confusion between bun-for-tests and node-for-consumer
expected_output.non_goals_explicit: Does not address Bun consumer adoption (out of scope per ADR-002 decision); does not model risk of Bun acquisitions or sunsetting (too speculative)
failure_modes_named: Bun 1.4.x introduces breaking change in --parallel worker IPC — partial test runs silently pass
bun test --timeout 30000 too short for new slow test added by a contributor — test passes locally with bun, fails in CI on slower runner
Node subtest shimming restored to single-process mode — reintroduces NotImplementedError on a CI config change

dependencies_graphed.ci_gate: GitHub Actions test.yml step 10: bun test --parallel
dependencies_graphed.bun_version_pin: package.json engines.bun: >=1.3.0 — lower bound only, no upper bound

expected_output.test_strategy_present: Revisit trigger: if bun test --parallel fails on Windows CI with >5% flake rate for 2 consecutive weeks, escalate to test:node fallback and re-evaluate
expected_output.tradeoffs_articulated: Pinning exact Bun version (1.3.14) prevents drift but forces manual bump for security fixes. Lower bound (>=1.3.0) allows auto-upgrade but risks silent breakage on minor bumps. ADR-002 chose lower bound + escape hatch as the right balance.

notes: Mined from ADR-002 (Bun runtime decision, 2026-06-10). Revisit triggers documented inline. Seed type: risk_premortem.
